topIssues.title: Archive node snapshots contain a gap in historical data
topIssues.author: JB273
topIssues.body:
Hi team,

We are using the snapshot from https://datadirs.optimism.io/ and it appears to be so that the provided snapshot here holds a gap for historical data.
We use the RPC mainly on The Graph indexing and we see the same missing data there (which is obvious), we have consulted with another indexer/RPC provider and they see the same issue.
It looks that the server from where the snapshot was created was in a pruning state (or was before)!

A couple of questions, can you confirm (and test);

1. If the snapshot should hold the complete historical data (from the bedrock block obviously)
2. Check if the data is available for the request attached from the snapshots provided by datadirs.optimism.io

We tested with this below curl request:
```
curl -sS "$RPC" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "jsonrpc":"2.0",
    "method":"eth_call",
    "params":[
      {
        "to":"0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006",
        "data":"0x18160ddd"
      },
      {
        "blockHash":"0x093a99185048338f9a43a0877d3d9d7b012aa2bc7007f632b3690758b778f49d"
      }
    ],
    "id":2
  }'
```
Response:
`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"state at block #127302882 is pruned"}}`

topIssues.title: flaky test: `XDM_MinGasLimits_Succeeds::invariant_minGasLimits`
topIssues.author: maurelian
topIssues.body:
https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/workflows/c9c37921-2268-4b12-a541-8034abfb303c (job `contracts-bedrock-tests-develop BRIDGE_HOOK`, [5757143](https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5757143))

Fails in about 1 in 6 `contracts-bedrock-tests-develop` jobs since #23619, which builds the contracts once and shares `cache/`, `artifacts/` and `forge-artifacts/` with the test jobs through the workspace. It did not fail before that change. It does not reproduce locally, and rerunning with the same `FOUNDRY_FUZZ_SEED` passes.

Every failure is a `relay` call with `value=1` that reverts with empty data ([`CrossDomainMessenger.t.sol#L84`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/bb389124e2da8aa1ddce029e29c3ca01bb40317a/packages/contracts-bedrock/test/invariants/CrossDomainMessenger.t.sol#L84)). Diagnostics on #23638 show the cause. When the relay reverts, the portal and `0x04` both have balance 0, although `setUp` deals the portal `type(uint128).max` ([L108](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/bb389124e2da8aa1ddce029e29c3ca01bb40317a/packages/contracts-bedrock/test/invariants/CrossDomainMessenger.t.sol#L108)) and 1 to 7 earlier value relays in the same run succeeded:

```
DIAG value=1 data=0x opBalance=0 idBalance=0 valueRelays=2
```

The balances drop to zero mid-run, but code and storage survive. That points to forge (1.8.3-dev) rather than the contracts.

A/B test on #23638:

| Arm | Failures |
|---|---|
| Shared build, default invariant workers | 5 of 24 |
| Shared build, `FOUNDRY_INVARIANT_WORKERS=1` | 1 of 6 |
| Compile in the test job (as before #23619) | 0 of 18 |

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topIssues.title: kona-node: --l1.trust-rpc can't be turned off from the CLI and only header hashes are checked
topIssues.author: 0xShadowX
topIssues.body:
Two problems with how kona-node checks what the L1 RPC returns.

`--l1.trust-rpc` and `--l2.trust-rpc` default to `true` ([providers.rs#L8-L25](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5315305/rust/kona/bin/node/src/flags/engine/providers.rs#L8-L25)) and are plain clap bool flags, so they can't be turned off from the command line. `--l1.trust-rpc=false` fails with `unexpected value 'false' for '--l1-trust-rpc' found; no more were expected`, and only `KONA_NODE_L1_TRUST_RPC=false` works. The help text says "If false, block hash verification is performed", but a CLI user can never get there.

Even with verification on, [`AlloyChainProvider`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5315305/rust/kona/crates/providers/providers-alloy/src/chain_provider.rs#L83-L105) only compares the header hash with the requested hash. The transactions returned by `block_info_and_transactions_by_hash` are not checked against `transactions_root`, and `receipts_by_hash` never looks at `receipts_root`. An RPC that serves the right header but drops or changes batcher transactions, or deposit and config logs, gets through.

For comparison, op-node defaults `--l1.trustrpc` to false. When it doesn't trust the RPC it checks the block hash and the transactions root (`RPCBlock.Verify`), and it always checks receipts against the receipts root (`validateReceipts`).

I'll open a PR that makes both flags accept `=false` and adds the transactions and receipts root checks when the RPC isn't trusted. Whether the L1 default should flip to false like op-node is probably your call, so the PR leaves the default alone.

topIssues.title: kona-node: signer updates can be missed when watch notifications coalesce
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
Kona's signer update channel is `watch<Address>`, which retains only the latest value. A verifier that owns its current/previous signer state can therefore miss intermediate rotations when updates arrive before it consumes the channel.

For example, if L1 observation publishes A -> B -> C while gossip still knows A, gossip observes only A -> C. It retains A as the previous signer instead of B: blocks from B are rejected, and A can receive grace even though it is no longer the immediately previous signer. A -> B -> A can be invisible as an address change. Delayed consumption also means the verifier starts its grace timer later than the producer observed the rotation.

The normal rotation grace-period fix in https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23626 intentionally keeps the existing address channels and tracks grace locally in the verifier. This issue tracks the notification/history limitation separately; it does not block that fix.

Investigate ordered rotation notifications or publishing sufficient rotation state and observation time to make coalescing safe. Also distinguish channel coalescing from intermediate onchain rotations that occur between L1 state reads: fixing the channel alone cannot recover history the producer never observed.

Regression coverage should include A -> B -> C before consumption, A -> B -> A, and a delayed consumer that must not extend the intended grace window.

Related: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22839

topPRs.title: kona-node!: start conductor-managed sequencers stopped
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Conductor-managed Kona sequencers can become active on process startup without coordinated activation when `--sequencer.stopped` is omitted. They now always start stopped and wait for an explicit start, including when constructed directly through Rust.

Tenth PR in the stack, based on #23627. Preserves the remaining startup protection from #23578; #23581 and #23223 already supply its leadership checks and disaster-recovery behavior. Review against the immediate parent.

BREAKING CHANGE: Operators configuring `--conductor.rpc` must activate through conductor coordination, or explicitly call `admin_overrideLeader` followed by `admin_startSequencer` during disaster recovery. Leaving `--sequencer.stopped` unset no longer starts a conductor-managed sequencer automatically.

Validation: all 316 tests across kona-node-service, kona-node, and lokahi pass with all features and zero skips. Full workspace Rust lint passes, including formatting, Clippy, nightly documentation, and upstream-mirror checks. Independent Rust and startup/API reviews have no outstanding findings. Full devnet acceptance tests were not rerun locally.

topPRs.title: kona-node,op-acceptance-tests: serve the safe head history and compare it with op-node
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #23583, which records the safe head history; review that first. This PR makes the record usable and proves it against op-node.

A kona-node started with `--safedb.path` (or `KONA_NODE_SAFEDB_PATH`) opens an on-disk safe head database and serves the two RPCs that proofs tooling reads from a rollup node. `optimism_safeHeadAtL1Block` was a stub answering method-not-found, which op-node's rollup client happens to read as an empty database; `superroot_atTimestamp` did not exist. Both answer in op-node's wire shape and with op-node's error messages, because that client recognizes a not-found answer by its message. A kona-node without the flag behaves as before, except that the stub now reports the database as not enabled instead of the method as missing. Combining the flag with derivation delegation is refused at startup, since a delegated node derives nothing and would serve a stale record.

Two differences from op-node surfaced only once the two ran side by side, and both are fixed here. op-node records the L2 genesis as safe from L1 block zero whenever derivation resets to genesis, so it answers for every L1 block below the first derived record; kona-node now does the same. And the super root preimage's timestamp is a hex quantity on the wire where the rest of the response uses plain integers.

The new `safeheaddb_parity` acceptance package runs an op-node verifier and a kona-node verifier on one chain, both recording, and asserts that every safe head answer and every super-root answer agree in both directions, through steady derivation, an L1 reorg, a kona-node CL restart, and a CL plus EL restart. It also checks that both nodes refuse the query the same way without a database. Written first, the package failed against the previous kona-node for exactly the reasons above; it passes against this branch locally. The mixed devstack runtime gained a per-node safe head database switch for it. The EL-resync scenario from #23585 is not in the package yet: kona-node clears its history when it resumes above the recorded tip (follow-up on #23474) and the devstack cannot wipe an op-reth data dir between a stop and a start.

Depends on #23514 for `CurrentL1`: kona-node reports the L1 head there today, where op-node reports the derivation origin, and op-challenger and op-proposer read that field from both RPCs' responses to decide whether a node is in sync. #23514 fixes it through the L1 watcher state that both RPCs here read from, so they inherit it with no change. It also touches the derivation actor constructor that #23583 changes, so this stack rebases onto develop once #23514 merges.

The `kona-gossip` commit is a cherry-pick of #23586 and disappears once that merges; without it kona-node cannot start on a host whose resolver configuration lists a scoped IPv6 nameserver, which is why the suite could not run here at first.

Closes #23475, closes #23476, closes #23477, closes #23585. Part of #23474, tracked under #23473.

Reviews run: `safedb-reviewer`, `rust-code-reviewer`, `go-code-reviewer`. Applied everything except: the `CurrentL1` finding is deferred to #23514 as above; the `kona-rpc` tests keep using the real rocksdb database rather than a stub, as the derivation actor tests already do; the suggestion to point the kona-sp1 decoders at these wire types is a follow-up. Reviewers should know `kona-rpc`'s test build now needs libclang locally.

topPRs.title: kona-node: support conductor disaster recovery
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Kona's admin_overrideLeader now bypasses conductor commits locally, allowing an operator to resume sequencing after quorum loss, matching op-node's recovery override. The separate conductor_overrideLeader(true) remains necessary for its leader-gated proxy traffic. This enables TestDisasterRecoveryLeaderOverride for Kona.

Fourth PR in the stack: #23220 → #23227 → #23229 → this PR. The preceding PR prevents canonicalization and gossip after a failed conductor commit, so this PR adds no start-time leadership check. The shared recovery test drops its startup-RPC rejection expectation and retains the override, resumed sequencing, proxy access, and proxy refusal assertions.

Validation: the actual Kona/op-reth conductor suite passes all 12 tests with zero skips; the revised recovery scenario also passes against op-node/op-reth. All 226 engine/service/RPC tests, full workspace Rust lint, and Go lint pass. Rust, Go, and deletion reviews have no unresolved findings.

topPRs.title: kona-engine!: retain completed safe checkpoints across resets
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
A same-height L1 replacement can rewind Kona’s safe head by roughly 70,000 L2 blocks even when its batch inputs remain canonical. Retain the newest completed safe checkpoint whose inherited L1 inputs and L2 ancestry still match, with fresh execution validation and chain-anchor rechecks. Resets retaining the confirmed safe head resume derivation immediately. Execution responses of `SYNCING` retry; `INVALID` and unexpected statuses stop recovery with execution diagnostics instead of retrying indefinitely.

Stacked on #23548; review this diff against that PR. Merge #23548 first, then restack this PR onto `develop`. The base provides op-node’s normal recovery rules. This PR adds only the checkpoint optimization, its replay/span safeguards, and its regression tests. Tracking stays inside the engine; SafeDB attribution is unchanged. Startup and unavailable history retain conservative recovery.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/328.

Validation: all 396 affected/dependent Rust tests pass with all features and zero skips. Full Rust workspace lint passes. Independent Rust/reorg reviews find no remaining issues. The combined implementation is preserved across the split.

BREAKING CHANGE: Exhaustive `SyncStartError` matches must handle `CheckpointNotValidated` by retrying while execution is syncing, and `CheckpointRejected` as a non-retryable execution failure carrying the full payload status. The public recovery function’s signature is unchanged.

topPRs.title: kona-node: commit sequenced payloads before canonicalization and gossip
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Kona commits each sequenced payload to the conductor before updating the canonical unsafe head or gossiping it. A rejected or timed-out commit now leaves the head unchanged, retains the build job, and retries getPayload after one second, matching op-node. Once a commit succeeds, temporary engine failures retry that exact committed payload; stale or invalid payloads are dropped, and expired build jobs are rebuilt. Derived-block processing retains its existing combined build/import flow.

Third PR in the stack: #23220 → #23227 → this PR → #23223. This supplies the publication gate used by the final recovery PR, which needs no start-time leadership check. Related: #21906; restart durability remains outside this change.

Validation: all 225 engine/service/RPC tests and full workspace Rust lint pass. Regression tests cover commit rejection and timeout, retry ordering, stale/invalid payloads, expired jobs, and unsafe-head notification before the canonicalization response. The actual Kona/op-reth conductor suite passes all 11 enabled tests, with disaster recovery intentionally skipped in this layer. Rust and deletion reviews have no unresolved findings.

A real paused-controller diagnostic forces a non-leader sequencer to run: eight rejected conductor commits leave the canonical head unchanged. The same diagnostic fails against the previous binary because its head advances before the rejected commit. The diagnostic source and logs are retained with the local validation artifacts.
